title: Forward contract model for GPU pools: cashflow & utilization scenarios
summary: A spreadsheet-style working model that treats reserved GPU commitments as forward contracts with phased delivery and optional early-exit. Simulates cashflow, utilization, hedging via on-demand top-up, and SLA buffer tradeoffs to inform pricing/discounting strategy for Dedicated capacity.

key_assumptions: Committed GPU fee monthly: reflects amortized capex + margin (example numbers only)
On-demand rate is per-GPU-hour; monthly on-demand spend calculated using peak hours * topup GPUs
BreakevenMonths computed as committed_outflow / (savings_vs_on_demand per month), approximate
Slack buffer: number of GPUs held to meet SLA targets and absorb variance
Buyout and phased delivery options change effective monthly outflow and create optionality value
sensitivity_checks: Vary on-demand rate +/-25% to test worst-case on-demand spend impact
Vary utilization +/-15 percentage points to identify utilization cliffs where reserved pool becomes net-loss
Test ramp schedules (immediate, 3-month phasing, 6-month phasing) to assess cashflow vs. savings tradeoff
Model early-exit penalties at 10%, 25%, 40% of remaining commit to price buyout option
analysis_notes: Key insight: a modest reduction in assumed avg utilization (from 0.65 to 0.50) turns a positive NPV reserved deal into a multi-quarter cash drag once on-demand top-up costs are included.
Buyout option priced conservatively (30% remaining value) materially reduces risk for customers with uncertain demand, enabling a higher initial sale conversion at slightly lower committed price.
Phased delivery (ramp-in) reduces near-term cash outflow but also reduces realized savings in early months; good for PLG customers with uncertain adoption curves.

Hedged-split (reserved + short spot offset) smooths peak cost exposure and preserves ability to serve rare spikes without overselling reserved pools. Operational complexity increases: routing, spot backfills, tracking.
Operational recommendation: instrument per-customer utilization telemetry and expose a recommended phasing template in the console during checkout to reduce mismatch risk.
recommended_pricing_variants: Standard-forward (12mo): baseline discounted rate; no buyout; tight SLA buffer (15-20 GPUs)
Phased-forward (12mo phased 3mo): 10% lower first-quarter fee; phased commitment schedule; higher monitoring requirements
Buyout-forward (12mo): slightly lower monthly fee, buyout at month 9 = 30% remaining commitment value
Hedged-forward (12mo + spot-offset): blended price with explicit spot-coverage discount; requires routing and telemetry; recommended for customers with bursty patterns

conclusion: Treating reserved commitments as forward contracts with optional phasing and buyout terms increases commercial flexibility and reduces churn risk. The model shows clear sensitivity to realized utilization and on-demand pricing; recommended product levers are phased commitments and a conservative buyout option to drive conversions while limiting downside for Redwood.
